docs.title: Documentation – Observability Stack (WEBCON)
docs.text:
A stack for analyzing WEBCON 2026.2+ performance: metrics, traces, and logs from the WEBCON Portal and WEBCON WorkFlow Service, SQL Server and Windows metrics, dashboards and alerts in Grafana. Everything runs as Windows services installed by a single PowerShell script.

Disclaimer. A private project shared as a demonstration of monitoring capabilities. It is not a WEBCON product and is not developed, supported, or endorsed by WEBCON. No support and no warranty – use at your own risk; test the solution before using it in a production environment. Details: MIT license (LICENSE). WEBCON, Grafana, and other names are trademarks of their respective owners.

Online: https://mmbednarz.github.io/observability-stack/ (one copy per release – version selector in the header). The same pages are in the docs folder of the release package for offline reading.

docs.title: Quick start – installation on a single machine (all-in-one)
docs.text:
This guide takes you from zero to working dashboards in Grafana when WEBCON, SQL Server, and the observability stack run on the same machine (a typical dev / test environment). It takes about 30 minutes, of which about 10 minutes are spent downloading and installing the components.

Stack on a separate machine (WEBCON and SQL on other hosts): Remote mode.

What you do not need to know: Prometheus, Grafana, Tempo, or OpenTelemetry. The installer configures everything on its own, and this guide tells you what you should see after each step.

docs.title: What gets installed
docs.text:
Five Windows services (names start with obs-) in the C:\Observability folder:

Service Purpose obs-alloy receives telemetry from WEBCON, collects Windows and SQL Server metrics obs-prometheus stores metrics (counters, durations, load) obs-tempo stores traces – the detailed course of individual WEBCON operations obs-loki stores WEBCON logs obs-grafana website with dashboards and alerts – http://localhost:3000

All services listen on 127.0.0.1 only – they are not visible from other computers (to change this: parameters, -GrafanaListenAll).

docs.title: Step 0. Check the requirements
docs.text:
• Windows Server 2019+ or Windows 10/11, an account with administrator privileges.
  • WEBCON 2026.2 or later (2026.1 is not supported).
  • Internet access from the server (GitHub, dl.grafana.com, grafana.com) – the installer downloads the components.
  • ~10 GB of free space on drive C:.
  • Free ports: 3000, 3100, 3200, 4317, 4318, 7947, 9090, 9096, 9097, 12345, 14317 (the installer checks them and reports any conflict).

Details and SQL Server preparation: Requirements and preparation.

docs.title: Step 1. Download the installation files
docs.text:
1. Download the latest observability-stack-<version>.zip package and the .sha256 file from the Releases page.
  2. Verify the checksum, unblock the archive (otherwise Windows blocks scripts downloaded from the internet), and extract it, e.g., to C:\Install:
(Get-FileHash .\observability-stack-0.12.1.zip -Algorithm SHA256).Hash   # compare with the .sha256 file
Unblock-File .\observability-stack-0.12.1.zip
Expand-Archive .\observability-stack-0.12.1.zip -DestinationPath C:\Install

Do not extract the package into the C:\Observability installation directory – the installer refuses (uninstalling with -RemoveFiles would delete it together with the data).

After installation, the package is no longer needed: the installer copies the scripts to C:\Observability\app (smoke test, uninstall, parameter changes, Set-WebconTelemetry.ps1, SQL scripts).

docs.title: Step 2. Prepare the SQL logins (recommended)
docs.text:
Without this step the stack works, but without the SQL Server dashboard and without some panels of the “WEBCON – Operations” dashboard. You can skip it and come back to it later (running the installer again adds SQL).

Two SQL logins are needed – details and scripts for the DBA: Requirements and preparation → SQL Server.

Login Purpose Script for the DBA svc_obs_mssql_exporter SQL Server metrics (load, locks, waits) sql\grant-sql-exporter-permissions.sql svc_obs_grafana_reader reading path names and active tasks from the WEBCON content database sql\grant-webcon-reader-permissions.sql

SQL Server Express: TCP is disabled by default, and the installer connects to SQL over TCP only. Enable TCP with a static port 1433 – instructions: Requirements → SQL Server Express.

docs.title: Step 3. Run the installer
docs.text:
Open PowerShell as administrator (right-click → Run as administrator) and go to the folder with the files:

cd C:\Install\observability-stack-0.12.1
Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process Bypass -Force

Choose one option:

# a) without SQL Server (simplest)
.\Install-ObservabilityStack.ps1 -SqlServer ''

# b) with SQL Server metrics – the installer asks for the login and password
.\Install-ObservabilityStack.ps1 -SqlServer 'localhost,1433' -SqlLogin svc_obs_mssql_exporter

# c) like b) + data from the WEBCON content database for the "WEBCON – Operations" dashboard (recommended)
.\Install-ObservabilityStack.ps1 -SqlServer 'localhost,1433' -SqlLogin svc_obs_mssql_exporter `
    -WebconSqlReaderLogin svc_obs_grafana_reader -WebconContentDatabase WEBCON_Content

localhost,1433 is the address of the SQL instance in host,port format. A named instance on a dynamic port (e.g., localhost\SQLEXPRESS) does not work – see the SQL Express note above.

What you will see: successive ==> … sections with [OK] lines. The installer:

  1. checks free ports and the permissions of the SQL logins (if permissions are missing, it prints commands for the DBA and stops),
  2. downloads the components and verifies their checksums,
  3. generates the configuration and the Grafana administrator password,
  4. registers and starts the obs-* services.

At the end, it prints a summary with addresses and – only on the first installation – the Grafana administrator password:

Summary
    Grafana     http://localhost:3000  (admin / password: C:\Observability\secrets\grafana-admin.txt)
                New admin password: ************************

Save the password in a password manager. Ingester not ready messages while Loki / Tempo start are normal – the installer waits until the components are ready.

docs.title: Step 4. Point WEBCON telemetry to the stack
docs.text:
By default, WEBCON does not send metrics, traces, or logs. The Set-WebconTelemetry.ps1 script enables this in the appsettings files of the Portal and the Service. Preview first:

.\scripts\Set-WebconTelemetry.ps1 -WhatIf

The script finds the files in C:\Program Files\WEBCON and C:\Program Files (x86)\WEBCON and lists what it will change. Then make the actual change:

.\scripts\Set-WebconTelemetry.ps1

After you confirm (Y), the script backs up the files (*.bak-<timestamp>), changes the configuration, and restarts the WEBCON WorkFlow Service and the Portal application – schedule this outside users' working hours. Details and rolling back the changes: WEBCON configuration.

docs.title: Step 5. Check that everything works
docs.text:
.\Test-ObservabilityStack.ps1

The smoke test sends a test trace, log, and metric and checks that they reached the data stores. Expected result (excerpt):

==> End-to-end OTLP flow
    [OK]   Tempo: test trace found
    [OK]   Loki: test log found
    [OK]   Prometheus: test metric found
==> WEBCON and host data (informational)
    [OK]   OTLP source: WebCon.WorkFlow
    [OK]   OTLP source: Portal
    [OK]   webcon_* metrics present
    [OK]   mssql exporter: up
==> Alerts
    [OK]   Alert rules loaded: 30
Result: OK
  • OTLP source: Portal appears only after the first visit to the Portal after the restart (IIS starts the application on the first request). Open the Portal in a browser and repeat the test after 2 minutes – WEBCON sends metrics every 60 s.
  • A [WARN] about the Loki “pattern ingester” is only a warning – it can last up to 2 h after startup.
  • Other problems: Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Step 6. Sign in to Grafana
docs.text:
1. Open http://localhost:3000.
  2. User admin, password from step 3. If you do not have it, read it in PowerShell as administrator:
Get-Content C:\Observability\secrets\grafana-admin.txt
  1. You will see the Start home screen – WEBCON status at a glance, links, and firing alerts. All dashboards: menu (☰) → Dashboards, in folders:
Folder Dashboard Where to start webcon WEBCON – Performance current performance: Portal, forms, paths, business rules, SQL, Service webcon WEBCON – Operations weekly overview: most frequent actions and paths, tasks, external APIs webcon WEBCON – Availability and backlog Portal availability (/health probe) and backlog in the content database sql SQL Server – WEBCON database load and problems host Windows – Host load CPU, memory, disks, processes

The first meaningful charts appear after users have worked in WEBCON for a dozen or so minutes. How to read the dashboards: Grafana in 10 minutes.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Other Grafana users: menu → Administration → Users and access → Users → New user (the Viewer role is enough for viewing).
  • Access to Grafana from other computers: reinstall with -GrafanaListenAll (Upgrade).
  • After a WEBCON upgrade: run C:\Observability\app\scripts\Set-WebconTelemetry.ps1 again (Upgrade).
  • New stack version: Upgrade.

docs.title: Server
docs.text: Requirement Details Operating system Windows Server 2019+ (verified on 2025) or Windows 10/11 (verified on 11). tar.exe is required (included in the system since Windows 10 1803 / Server 2019) PowerShell Windows PowerShell 5.1 (built-in) or PowerShell 7+ Permissions local administrator – installing Windows services, writing to C:\Observability, reading secrets Internet github.com, objects.githubusercontent.com, dl.grafana.com, grafana.com (community dashboards). Proxy: configure it in the system before installation Disk ~1 GB of binaries + data: depends on traffic and retention, on dev usually < 10 GB Memory about 2–3 GB of RAM for all stack services (Alloy has a 1 GiB limit, parameter -AlloyMemoryLimit) WEBCON 2026.2+ (Portal and Service). 2026.1 is not supported – different span names, panels based on traces would be empty

docs.title: Ports (127.0.0.1 only)
docs.text:
Port Component Port Component 3000 Grafana 9090 Prometheus 4317 / 4318 Alloy – OTLP receiver (gRPC / HTTP) for WEBCON 9096 Loki gRPC 12345 Alloy – UI 3100 Loki HTTP 3200 Tempo HTTP 9097 / 14317 / 7947 Tempo gRPC / OTLP / memberlist

The installer checks the ports before installation and prints the process that occupies a port (e.g., a local Jaeger, Seq, or another OTLP collector). In local mode, no firewall rules are needed.

docs.title: SQL Server
docs.text: SQL Server metrics and panels based on the WEBCON database are optional. Two separate SQL logins are needed (SQL authentication, not Windows):

docs.title: 1. Metrics exporter login – svc_obs_mssql_exporter
docs.text:
Collects server metrics (load, waits, locks, I/O, memory). It needs only VIEW SERVER STATE and VIEW ANY DEFINITION – without access to WEBCON data and without sysadmin.

The DBA runs in SSMS:

CREATE LOGIN [svc_obs_mssql_exporter] WITH PASSWORD = N'<strong_password>', CHECK_POLICY = ON, DEFAULT_DATABASE = [master];
-- then the script from the repository:
-- sql\grant-sql-exporter-permissions.sql

Checking the login without installing: .\scripts\Test-SqlExporterLogin.ps1.

docs.title: 2. Grafana login to the content database – svc_obs_grafana_reader
docs.text:
The “WEBCON – Operations” dashboard shows the names of paths and processes (traces contain only IDs) and the current active tasks. The login gets SELECT on only 5 tables: ActiveTasks, WFAvaiblePaths, WFSteps, WorkFlows, WFDefinitions – without access to form data.

CREATE LOGIN [svc_obs_grafana_reader] WITH PASSWORD = N'<strong_password>', CHECK_POLICY = ON, DEFAULT_DATABASE = [master];
-- then the script from the repository (set the content database names in the header, default WEBCON_Content):
-- sql\grant-webcon-reader-permissions.sql

A WEBCON upgrade can recreate the tables and remove the permissions – after a WEBCON upgrade, the DBA runs this script again.

Why two logins: any dashboard editor can write queries against the Grafana data source, and the exporter login can see the query text of other sessions (VIEW SERVER STATE). The Grafana login therefore has a minimal scope.

docs.title: 3. Metrics from the content database (optional)
docs.text:
Backlog that is not visible in WEBCON telemetry: overdue timeouts, cyclical actions with errors, the email queue, sizes of queue and log tables (the “WEBCON – Availability and backlog” dashboard, alerts D1–D3). Enabled with the installer parameter -WebconDbMetrics $true; requires SQL metrics (the exporter login).

The exporter login (svc_obs_mssql_exporter) gets a user in the content database and SELECT only on the columns used in the queries (IDs, statuses, counters, dates) – without email and form content. The DBA runs the script from the repository (set the login and the content database names in the header):

-- sql\grant-webcon-db-metrics.sql
DECLARE @login     sysname       = N'svc_obs_mssql_exporter';
DECLARE @databases nvarchar(max) = N'WEBCON_Content';

Missing permissions do not stop the installation – the installer prints a warning, and the metrics appear once the permissions are granted (without reinstalling). After a WEBCON upgrade, run the script again.

docs.title: SQL Server Express – enabling TCP
docs.text:
The exporter connects to SQL Server over TCP only. SQL Server Express has TCP and the SQL Browser service disabled by default, so the localhost\SQLEXPRESS address does not work. Enable TCP with a static port:

  1. SQL Server Configuration Manager → SQL Server Network Configuration → Protocols for SQLEXPRESS.
  2. TCP/IP → Enabled = Yes.
  3. TCP/IP → Properties → IP Addresses tab → IPAll section: TCP Dynamic Ports = empty, TCP Port = 1433.
  4. Restart the SQL Server (SQLEXPRESS) service – this drops connections, including WEBCON's.
  5. Check: sqlcmd -S localhost,1433 -E -C -Q "SELECT @@VERSION".

Windows Firewall rules are not needed when SQL and the stack are on the same machine. In the installer, specify -SqlServer 'localhost,1433'.

docs.title: Before installation – checklist
docs.text:
• PowerShell running as administrator
  • release package files extracted and unblocked (Unblock-File on the ZIP)
  • (optional) SQL logins created, passwords at hand
  • (SQL Express) TCP enabled on port 1433
  • maintenance window for restarting WEBCON (the Set-WebconTelemetry.ps1 step)

Next: Quick start, step 3.

docs.title: WEBCON configuration (Set-WebconTelemetry.ps1)
docs.text: WEBCON 2026.2+ has built-in OpenTelemetry support, but it does not send any data by default. The scripts\Set-WebconTelemetry.ps1 script enables export to the local Alloy (http://localhost:4318).

docs.title: What the script changes
docs.text:
1. In C:\Program Files\WEBCON and C:\Program Files (x86)\WEBCON, it finds the appsettings.json / appsettings.Production.json files with an OpenTelemetry section (usually the Portal and the Service). When a directory contains appsettings.Production.json, only that file is changed.
  2. In the OpenTelemetry section, it:
  3. enables Metrics, Tracing, Logs,
  4. sets the OTLP/HTTP exporter to http://localhost:4318/v1/metrics|traces|logs,
  5. disables other exporters in these sections (unless -KeepOtherExporters is specified),
  6. enables SQL query tracing (SqlTracing) – short queries are then dropped by Alloy (by default < 1 s).
  7. It sets the OTEL_* environment variables (metric exemplars, span event limit) and the component marker OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=webcon.component=… (other attributes in this variable are kept):
  8. Service – in the Windows service registry key (webcon.component=service),
  9. Portal (IIS) – in web.config (<aspNetCore><environmentVariables>, webcon.component=portal).

Based on the marker, Alloy assigns the services the fixed names Portal and WebCon.WorkFlow, which are used by the dashboards and alerts – regardless of ServiceName in the WEBCON appsettings (it can differ between installations). The name from WEBCON is kept in the webcon.service.name.original attribute. 4. It restarts the WEBCON WorkFlow Service; saving web.config restarts the Portal application.

Before each change, it creates a backup copy of the file: appsettings.Production.json.bak-20261106101500, web.config.bak-….

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# preview – changes nothing
.\scripts\Set-WebconTelemetry.ps1 -WhatIf

# apply (asks for confirmation, restarts WEBCON)
.\scripts\Set-WebconTelemetry.ps1
Parameter When to use -SqlTracing Threshold (default) / All / Off SQL query tracing: slow (installer threshold), all, disabled. All also requires the installer with -SqlSpanThresholdSeconds 0 -AppSettingsPath <file> change only selected files -SearchRoot <directory> WEBCON in a non-standard directory (default: Program Files\WEBCON and Program Files (x86)\WEBCON) -NoRestart change without a restart – takes effect after the next WEBCON restart -RestartIis full iisreset instead of restarting only the application -Force no confirmation prompt (automated scripts) -DisableLogs do not send logs

The installer can run the script itself: Install-ObservabilityStack.ps1 … -ConfigureWebcon.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• .\Test-ObservabilityStack.ps1 → section “WEBCON and host data”: OTLP source: WebCon.WorkFlow (Service), OTLP source: Portal and WEBCON service names normalized (webcon.component).
  • [WARN] WEBCON service with a non-standard name … or … telemetry without the webcon.component marker – WEBCON sends telemetry without the marker (e.g. configured manually). Run the script again; when that is not possible, use the fallback name-based mapping: the installer with -WebconPortalServiceName / -WebconServiceServiceName (parameters).
  • The Portal appears only after the first request (open the Portal in a browser); WEBCON metrics arrive every 60 s.

docs.title: Reverting the changes
docs.text:
Restore the backup copies and restart WEBCON:

$dir = 'C:\Program Files\WEBCON\WEBCON BPS WorkFlow Service'
Get-ChildItem $dir -Filter 'appsettings.Production.json.bak-*' | Sort-Object Name | Select-Object -Last 1 |
    Copy-Item -Destination (Join-Path $dir 'appsettings.Production.json') -Force
Restart-Service 'WebCon WorkFlow Service'

Do the same for the Portal directory (WEBCON BPS Portal: appsettings.Production.json and web.config). If the script was run several times, choose the backup copy from before the first run (the oldest one).

docs.title: Known issues in WEBCON 2026.2.5
docs.text: Symptom Cause / workaround WEBCON does not start after manually editing appsettings "Headers": "" in an exporter breaks the startup (IndexOutOfRangeException) – the script never writes an empty Headers. Every log entry appears twice a second sink with the default configuration sends logs as unknown_service:… – Alloy drops them. Database connection details in traces Alloy removes the webcon.db.cs attribute (database connection details) from spans; the smoke test checks this. The Service does not start within 30 s (event 7009) the Service startup can be close to the SCM limit – this also happens without telemetry; start it again

docs.title: Remote mode – stack on a separate machine
docs.text:
You install the stack (Grafana, Prometheus, Tempo, Loki) on a separate, empty VM. The WEBCON and SQL Server hosts run only a lightweight agent (the obs-alloy service) that collects data and sends it to the stack.

WEBCON host                                    Stack VM
  Portal / Service ─OTLP─> agent obs-alloy ──TCP 4317 (traces, logs)──> Alloy ─> Tempo / Loki / Prometheus
  Windows / IIS metrics ─┘                 └─TCP 9999 (metrics)───────>          Grafana :3000
SQL host
  Windows + SQL metrics ─> agent obs-alloy ──TCP 9999──────────────>
  SQL Server <──────────────── TCP 1433 ── Grafana ("WEBCON SQL" data source)

When to choose it: a production-like environment, WEBCON and SQL on different servers, no approval for additional services on the WEBCON server other than the agent.

Status: the mode has been verified on a single VM with a simulated agent. Agent installation on real WEBCON / SQL hosts has not been tested yet – please report problems.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Stack VM: as in Requirements; internet access is needed only on the stack VM (the agent bundle contains the binaries).
  • Network connectivity:
From To Port Purpose WEBCON host, SQL host stack VM TCP 4317 traces and logs (OTLP gRPC) WEBCON host, SQL host stack VM TCP 9999 metrics stack VM SQL host TCP 1433 (-SqlPort) “WEBCON SQL” data source in Grafana users' browsers stack VM TCP 3000 Grafana (-GrafanaListenAll)
  • On the hosts: local administrator; on the SQL host, a Windows account with the sysadmin role (the script creates logins and grants permissions).
  • Agent → stack connections use no TLS and no authentication; the stack VM firewall allows only the host addresses. Filters (including removal of the webcon.db.cs attribute from traces) already run in the agent.

docs.title: Step 1. Stack VM – install the stack and the agent bundle
docs.text:
.\Install-ObservabilityStack.ps1 -WebconHost WEBCON01 -SqlHost SQL01 -SqlInstanceName SQLEXPRESS -PortalUrl https://bps.example.com -GrafanaListenAll
Parameter Meaning -WebconHost name of the WEBCON host (Portal + Service) -SqlHost name of the SQL Server host with the WEBCON databases -SqlInstanceName instance name (MSSQLSERVER = default instance) -SqlPort TCP port of the instance (default: 1433) -WebconContentDatabase content database (default: WEBCON_Content) -PortalUrl main Portal address for the availability probe (without the parameter the installer asks); the probe is run by the agent on the WEBCON host, connecting locally -CentralAddress stack VM address used by the agents (default: FQDN) -AgentAddress IP addresses allowed in the firewall (default: from DNS of the host names)

The installer creates the C:\Observability\agent-bundle bundle and the agent-bundle.zip archive with:

  • README.txt – the order of steps with the names of your hosts,
  • 01-Sql-SQL01.ps1, 02-Webcon-WEBCON01.ps1 – ready-to-run scripts for the hosts (WEBCON and SQL on one host: a single 01-WebconSql-<host>.ps1 script),
  • Alloy and WinSW binaries, SQL scripts, Set-WebconTelemetry.ps1,
  • SQL login passwords (secrets\sql-logins.json) – the bundle is confidential; delete it from the hosts after installation.

docs.title: Step 2. SQL host
docs.text:
Copy agent-bundle.zip to the SQL host, extract it, and run PowerShell as administrator in the bundle directory:

Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process Bypass -Force
.\01-Sql-SQL01.ps1

The script creates the svc_obs_mssql_exporter and svc_obs_grafana_reader logins, grants permissions, installs the agent (Windows + SQL Server metrics) and adds a firewall rule for Grafana.

When TCP is disabled for the instance (typical for SQL Express), the script stops with a message. In that case:

.\01-Sql-SQL01.ps1 -EnableSqlTcp     # WARNING: restarts the SQL Server instance

docs.title: Step 3. WEBCON host
docs.text:
Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process Bypass -Force
.\02-Webcon-WEBCON01.ps1

The script installs the agent (receives WEBCON telemetry on 127.0.0.1:4318, Windows and IIS metrics, Portal /health probe) and runs Set-WebconTelemetry.ps1 – it restarts the WEBCON WorkFlow Service and the Portal application (with confirmation; -Force without prompting, -SkipWebconConfig without changing WEBCON).

The order “SQL first, then WEBCON” lets you fit both outages (SQL restart, WEBCON restart) into a single maintenance window.

docs.title: Step 4. Stack VM – verification
docs.text:
.\Test-ObservabilityStack.ps1

The “Remote agents” section checks host metrics, SQL metrics, WEBCON telemetry and a test log sent by the agent. Portal telemetry appears after the first visit to the Portal.

Finally, delete the bundle (agent-bundle, agent-bundle.zip) from the WEBCON and SQL hosts – the agent script copies everything needed later (uninstallation, Set-WebconTelemetry.ps1, SQL scripts) to C:\Observability\app on the host, without passwords. Do not extract the bundle to C:\Observability – the script will refuse to run.

docs.title: Upgrades and changes
docs.text:
• Running the stack installer again without -WebconHost / -SqlHost keeps the hosts and passwords (the bundle is regenerated with the same passwords).
  • Agent upgrade: after the stack is upgraded to a new version, the installer generates a new agent bundle (with the same version) → run the host script again (the script is idempotent).
  • Returning to local mode: .\Install-ObservabilityStack.ps1 -WebconHost '' -SqlHost ''.
  • Removing the agent from a host: Uninstall → agent.

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text: The installer is idempotent: running it again on an installed stack upgrades the binaries, configuration, dashboards and alert rules, and keeps the data (metrics, traces, logs, Grafana users) and secrets.

docs.title: Upgrading to a new version
docs.text:
1. Download the new package from Releases, unblock it and extract it to a new directory (e.g. C:\Install\observability-stack-0.12.1) – as in Quick start, step 1.
  2. Read the section of the new version in CHANGELOG.md (in the package) – Requires action lists the manual steps (e.g. new SQL permissions, running Set-WebconTelemetry.ps1 again).
  3. PowerShell as administrator, in the new package directory:
Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process Bypass -Force
.\Install-ObservabilityStack.ps1 -NonInteractive
C:\Observability\app\Test-ObservabilityStack.ps1

The installer shows the version change (Upgrading 0.12.0 -> 0.12.1), keeps the settings and data, and replaces C:\Observability\app with the scripts of the new version. You can delete the old and the new package afterwards. The installed version is shown by the smoke test (the “Version” section).

A version older than the installed one – the installer stops (the configuration and alert rules of the newer version may not match the older one). Deliberate return to an older version: -AllowDowngrade.

Tempo 3 (version 0.11.0 and later) – no way back below 0.11.0. The upgrade from 0.10.x replaces Tempo 2.10 with Tempo 3.1.1 automatically (traces from before the upgrade remain available). Tempo 2.10 cannot read the blocks written by Tempo 3, so installing a version older than 0.11.0 on 0.11.0+ requires deleting the trace data (C:\Observability\data\tempo, with the services stopped) – all traces are lost. If you may need to go back, copy data\tempo before the upgrade. Downtime: the installer stops the obs-* services for the duration of the upgrade (usually 1–3 minutes, longer when it downloads new component versions). WEBCON works normally – telemetry from this period is lost, WEBCON is not affected.

docs.title: Which settings are kept
docs.text:
All settings of the stack are kept (saved in C:\Observability\config\install-settings.json). Rule: a parameter specified explicitly > the value from the previous installation > the default value. An upgrade with -NonInteractive alone keeps the whole configuration:

  • SQL exporter instance and login (-SqlServer, -SqlLogin) + password; login, instance and database of the “WEBCON SQL” data source + password,
  • network access (-GrafanaListenAll, -OtlpListenAll) and the firewall rules,
  • retention (-RetentionMetricsDays, -RetentionTracesDays, -RetentionLogsDays), -SqlSpanThresholdSeconds, -AlloyMemoryLimit, -EnvironmentName, -ServiceLogPath, service name mapping, -SkipCommunityDashboards,
  • Portal probe (-PortalProbe, -PortalUrl, -ProbeUrl), database metrics (-WebconDbMetrics),
  • remote mode: hosts, instance, port, addresses, login passwords; the Grafana administrator password.

The installer lists the values different from the defaults that it took over, e.g. Kept from the previous installation: -GrafanaListenAll, -RetentionMetricsDays 90. The full list with the Kept column: Installer parameters.

Not kept (actions for a single run): -NonInteractive, -ForceDownload, -AllowDowngrade, -ConfigureWebcon. Always specify the same -Root (the settings file is in it).

Upgrade from 0.11.0 or older: the values that these versions did not save (network access, metrics and logs retention, Alloy memory limit) are read from the current configuration of the stack.

docs.title: What an upgrade overwrites
docs.text:
• Dashboards from the package (dashboards\) – changes made in Grafana to these dashboards will be lost. Save your own dashboards as new ones (Save as) – they are stored in the Grafana database and an upgrade does not touch them.
  • Alert rules – they are read-only in Grafana; a change = editing the YAML in config-templates\ (overwritten by the next release).
  • .json files in C:\Observability\config\grafana\dashboards that are not part of the package are deleted.
  • Component configuration in C:\Observability\config – regenerated from the templates.

docs.title: Changing parameters
docs.text:
Run the installer again with new parameters – without the package, from the copy in C:\Observability\app (the same version), e.g.:

cd C:\Observability\app
.\Install-ObservabilityStack.ps1 -GrafanaListenAll

Examples:

Goal Command add SQL metrics after an installation without SQL .\Install-ObservabilityStack.ps1 -SqlServer 'localhost,1433' -SqlLogin svc_obs_mssql_exporter add the “WEBCON SQL” data source .\Install-ObservabilityStack.ps1 -WebconSqlReaderLogin svc_obs_grafana_reader change the SQL exporter login password .\Install-ObservabilityStack.ps1 -SqlServer 'localhost,1433' -SqlLogin svc_obs_mssql_exporter (prompts for the password) disable SQL metrics .\Install-ObservabilityStack.ps1 -SqlServer '' disable the “WEBCON SQL” data source .\Install-ObservabilityStack.ps1 -WebconSqlReaderLogin '' Grafana accessible from the network .\Install-ObservabilityStack.ps1 -GrafanaListenAll (adds a firewall rule for port 3000) Grafana accessible only locally again .\Install-ObservabilityStack.ps1 -GrafanaListenAll:$false (removes the firewall rule) longer trace retention .\Install-ObservabilityStack.ps1 -RetentionTracesDays 14

The other settings stay unchanged – specify only the parameter you change.

Full list: Installer parameters.

docs.title: After a WEBCON upgrade
docs.text:
A WEBCON upgrade can overwrite appsettings and web.config and recreate content database tables:

  1. C:\Observability\app\scripts\Set-WebconTelemetry.ps1 – enables telemetry export again (WEBCON restart).
  2. DBA: C:\Observability\app\sql\grant-webcon-reader-permissions.sql – grants the permissions to the Grafana login again.
  3. C:\Observability\app\Test-ObservabilityStack.ps1 – verification.

Symptom of skipping these steps: empty WEBCON dashboards (step 1 missing) or errors in panels with path names and tasks (step 2 missing).

docs.title: Changing a component version (advanced)
docs.text: The versions of Grafana, Prometheus, Tempo, Loki and Alloy are pinned in versions.psd1 (URL + SHA256 checksum) and change with stack releases. Do not change them on the server – the configuration may require changes (e.g. Tempo 3.x removes the ingester / compactor sections).

docs.title: Grafana administrator password
docs.text:
The C:\Observability\secrets\grafana-admin.txt file is used only on the first start of Grafana (database creation). A password changed later in Grafana (Profile → Change password) is not saved in the file – the file will be out of date, and the smoke test will not check alerts. Recommendation: do not change the admin password; create separate accounts for people.

Resetting a forgotten password (PowerShell as administrator):

& C:\Observability\bin\Grafana\bin\grafana.exe cli --homepath C:\Observability\bin\Grafana `
    --config C:\Observability\config\grafana\grafana.ini admin reset-admin-password (Get-Content C:\Observability\secrets\grafana-admin.txt)

docs.title: Order
docs.text:
1. Disable telemetry in WEBCON – otherwise WEBCON will keep trying to send data to localhost:4318 (no impact on how WEBCON works, but with export errors in the logs).
  2. Remove the stack (Uninstall-ObservabilityStack.ps1).
  3. (optional) Remove the SQL logins.

docs.title: 1. WEBCON – restoring the configuration
docs.text:
Restore the backup copies of the files from before the first run of Set-WebconTelemetry.ps1 (the oldest *.bak-*) – procedure: WEBCON configuration → Reverting the changes. Files:

Directory (default: C:\Program Files\WEBCON\…) Files WEBCON BPS Portal appsettings.Production.json, web.config WEBCON BPS WorkFlow Service appsettings.Production.json

The OTEL_* variables of the Service are in the service registry key – remove them if you restore the configuration manually:

$key = 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\WebCon WorkFlow Service'
(Get-ItemProperty $key).Environment      # preview
Remove-ItemProperty $key -Name Environment   # only when it contains just the OTEL_* variables added by the script
Restart-Service 'WebCon WorkFlow Service'

A simpler alternative without restoring files: in appsettings.Production.json of the Portal and the Service, set OpenTelemetry › Metrics / Tracing / Logs › Enabled = false and restart WEBCON.

docs.title: 2. Removing the stack
docs.text:
PowerShell as administrator, in the C:\Observability\app directory (copy of the scripts of the installed version) or in the package directory:

# services and firewall rules; data, configuration and secrets REMAIN in C:\Observability
.\Uninstall-ObservabilityStack.ps1

# everything, including data and passwords (irreversible)
.\Uninstall-ObservabilityStack.ps1 -RemoveFiles
Variant When What remains without -RemoveFiles temporary shutdown, relocation, reinstallation keeping the history C:\Observability (data, secrets, install-settings.json). Running Install-ObservabilityStack.ps1 again restores the previous configuration and data with -RemoveFiles permanent removal, clean reinstallation nothing – a new installation requires the SQL logins and passwords again; Grafana gets a new admin password

Preview without changes: -WhatIf.

-RemoveFiles safeguards:

  • the installation directory contains a git repository (e.g. cloned into C:\Observability\...) – the script refuses to remove it; move the repository and run the script again,
  • the installation directory contains files other than the stack (bin, config, data, logs, services, secrets, downloads, app, agent-bundle) – the script lists them and asks for confirmation; -Force skips the prompt.

Clean reinstallation (e.g. to test a new version): Uninstall-ObservabilityStack.ps1 -RemoveFiles, then Quick start, step 3. The WEBCON configuration does not need to be changed – the localhost:4318 address stays the same.

docs.title: 3. SQL logins (optional)
docs.text:
The scripts do not remove the logins. DBA:

DROP LOGIN [svc_obs_mssql_exporter];
-- in each WEBCON content database:
USE [WEBCON_Content]; DROP USER IF EXISTS [svc_obs_grafana_reader];
DROP LOGIN [svc_obs_grafana_reader];

docs.title: Remote mode – removing the agent
docs.text:
On each WEBCON / SQL host (PowerShell as administrator, in C:\Observability\app – copy of the agent scripts; the agent bundle is not needed):

.\Uninstall-ObservabilityAgent.ps1               # obs-alloy service
.\Uninstall-ObservabilityAgent.ps1 -RemoveFiles  # also C:\Observability on the host

The script also removes the Observability - SQL (Grafana) firewall rule on the SQL host. It does not change the WEBCON configuration (step 1 – on the WEBCON host) or the SQL logins (it prints the DROP LOGIN commands).

On the stack VM: Uninstall-ObservabilityStack.ps1 also removes the Observability - Agenci rule.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Always start with the smoke test (PowerShell as administrator, repository directory):

.\Test-ObservabilityStack.ps1

then the service log Loki: pattern ingester not ready yet (WARN) an internal Loki module takes up to ~2 h to start nothing – logs are accepted End-to-end OTLP flow: test trace / log / metric not found Alloy does not pass data to the storage Alloy UI http://localhost:12345 (components in red), Application event log, source Alloy Tempo: TraceQL metrics error parquet corrupted Tempo block index procedure below WEBCON and host data: no OTLP source: Portal the Portal has not sent anything yet open the Portal in a browser, wait 2 min no OTLP source: WebCon.WorkFlow / webcon_* metrics WEBCON does not send telemetry Set-WebconTelemetry.ps1;
