docs.title: Installation problems
docs.text: Symptom Solution Ports in use: … the installer shows the process using the port – stop it (e.g. a local Jaeger, Seq, another OTLP collector) the script does not run / “is not digitally signed” Unblock-File on the downloaded ZIP before extracting; Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process Bypass -Force garbled special characters in messages the script file was changed with an editor that does not keep the BOM – download the files again download error / SHA256 mismatch no internet access or a proxy; retry with -ForceDownload SQL login verification failed the installer lists the missing permissions – pass them on to the DBA Grafana does not start after an upgrade C:\Observability\logs\grafana\grafana.log – Failed to provision alerting = an error in the alert rules from the repository

docs.title: WEBCON problems
docs.text: Symptom Solution WEBCON does not start after Set-WebconTelemetry.ps1 restore the *.bak-* backup copies (reverting); you can see the error by running WebCon.WorkFlow.Bootstrapper.exe from a console in the Service directory Portal panels are empty, and Service panels show Portal routes service names from appsettings instead of the fixed Portal / WebCon.WorkFlow – run Set-WebconTelemetry.ps1 (webcon.component marker); No appsettings files with an OpenTelemetry section found = WEBCON outside Program Files[ (x86)]\WEBCON → -SearchRoot WEBCON dashboards are empty after a WEBCON upgrade the upgrade overwrote appsettings – run Set-WebconTelemetry.ps1 again no slow SQL queries in traces SQL spans shorter than the threshold (default: 1 s) are dropped – this is intended; the installer's -SqlSpanThresholdSeconds

docs.title: Where the logs are
docs.text: Component Log Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, Tempo C:\Observability\logs\<component>\ (*.out.log, *.err.log; Grafana: grafana.log) Alloy Event Viewer → Application, source Alloy (not files), and the UI at http://localhost:12345 WinSW services C:\Observability\logs\<component>\*.wrapper.log installation configuration C:\Observability\config\install-settings.json

docs.title: Corrupted Tempo index
docs.text:
Symptom: the “Where the time goes” panels and other TraceQL-based panels show reading parquet file metadata: missing required field; smoke test: Tempo: TraceQL metrics error.

Stop-Service obs-tempo -Force          # also stops obs-alloy (dependency)
Remove-Item C:\Observability\data\tempo\blocks\single-tenant\index.json.gz, `
            C:\Observability\data\tempo\blocks\single-tenant\index.pb.zst -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Start-Service obs-tempo, obs-alloy

Tempo rebuilds the index from the blocks; no data is lost. In versions up to 0.10.0 (Tempo 2.10) the index was corrupted repeatedly on Windows (a Tempo 2.x bug) – the upgrade to 0.11.0 (Tempo 3) removes the cause; the procedure remains for any other index error.

docs.title: Components directly (diagnostics)
docs.text: Address What it shows http://localhost:12345 Alloy – processing graph, component status http://localhost:9090/query?g0.expr=up Prometheus – up = 1 for each metrics source scraped by Alloy (windows, mssql, stack components) http://localhost:3200/ready, http://localhost:3100/ready Tempo, Loki readiness

docs.title: Installer parameters (Install-ObservabilityStack.ps1)
docs.text:
The parameters are also described in the script header (.PARAMETER); syntax list: Get-Help .\Install-ObservabilityStack.ps1.

The Kept column – whether the installer uses the previous value when run again without the parameter (Upgrade). “No” = the default value is restored. A kept switch is disabled with -Name:$false (e.g. -GrafanaListenAll:$false).

docs.title: Basic
docs.text: Parameter Default Kept Description -Root C:\Observability – installation directory (always specify the same one) -EnvironmentName computer name yes environment label in telemetry -NonInteractive – – no prompts – missing values = error (automated scripts) -ConfigureWebcon – – after installation, runs scripts\Set-WebconTelemetry.ps1 (OpenTelemetry configuration in WEBCON appsettings) -AllowDowngrade – – allows installing a version older than the installed one (without this switch, a downgrade stops the installation) -ForceDownload – – downloads the components again (instead of using C:\Observability\downloads) -SkipCommunityDashboards – yes no ASP.NET Core dashboards from grafana.com

docs.title: SQL Server – metrics
docs.text: Parameter Default Kept Description -SqlServer prompt yes SQL Server instance to monitor, recommended in the host,port format (e.g. localhost,1433); a server name or server\instance also works if the instance is reachable over TCP (named instance: SQL Browser running); '' = no SQL Server metrics -SqlLogin prompt yes dedicated SQL login for the exporter (permissions) -SqlPassword prompt yes (secret) SecureString, e.g. (Read-Host -AsSecureString) -SqlEncrypt / -SqlTrustServerCertificate $true / $true no connection encryption / accepting the certificate without validation

docs.title: SQL Server – “WEBCON SQL” data source (content database)
docs.text: Parameter Default Kept Description -WebconSqlReaderLogin – yes read-only SQL login (permissions); '' = no data source -WebconSqlReaderPassword prompt yes (secret) SecureString -WebconSqlServer -SqlServer yes SQL Server instance hosting the content database -WebconContentDatabase WEBCON_Content yes content database name

docs.title: Availability and WEBCON database metrics
docs.text: Parameter Default Kept Description -PortalProbe $true yes Portal /health availability probe (in remote mode: the agent on the WEBCON host) -PortalUrl prompt yes main Portal address, the one users open, e.g. https://bps.example.com. The probe connects locally on the Portal server and verifies the certificate for the host name from this address. The installer asks, suggesting the address from an IIS binding with a host name; with -NonInteractive it uses that address, and when the bindings have no host name (*) it skips the probe with a warning. ' = detection from IIS -ProbeUrl – yes additional HTTP(S) addresses to check (2xx code), e.g. the production Portal; '' = no additional addresses -WebconDbMetrics $false yes metrics from the content database (-WebconContentDatabase): overdue timeouts, cyclical actions, emails, queue and log tables; permissions: sql\grant-webcon-db-metrics.sql

docs.title: Telemetry and retention
docs.text: Parameter Default Kept Description -SqlSpanThresholdSeconds 1 yes SQL query spans shorter than the threshold are dropped; 0 = keep all (high volume) -RetentionMetricsDays 15 yes how many days to keep metrics -RetentionTracesDays 8 yes traces (the “WEBCON – Operations” dashboard shows 7 days) -RetentionLogsDays 7 yes logs -AlloyMemoryLimit 1GiB yes Alloy memory limit -WebconPortalServiceName / -WebconServiceServiceName – yes fallback service name mapping: the name (ServiceName from WEBCON appsettings) under which the Portal / Service sends telemetry without the webcon.component marker; Alloy replaces it with Portal / WebCon.WorkFlow. Not needed after Set-WebconTelemetry.ps1; the values must differ; '' = no mapping -ServiceLogPath – yes glob pattern of the Service log files (e.g. D:\WEBCON\Service\Logs\*.log) – only for a Service without OTLP log export (WEBCON 2026.2 exports logs, do not use)

docs.title: Network
docs.text: Parameter Default Kept Description -GrafanaListenAll – yes Grafana on all interfaces + firewall rule Observability - Grafana (TCP 3000, Domain/Private profiles); -GrafanaListenAll:$false = localhost only, the rule is removed -OtlpListenAll – yes OTLP reception from the network (WEBCON on another machine without an agent) + rule Observability - OTLP; -OtlpListenAll:$false = disable, the rule is removed

docs.title: Remote mode
docs.text:
Description: Remote mode.

Parameter Default Kept Description -WebconHost / -SqlHost – yes agent hosts; '' for both = return to local mode -SqlInstanceName MSSQLSERVER yes instance name on -SqlHost -SqlPort 1433 yes TCP port of the instance -CentralAddress stack VM FQDN yes stack address written to the agent configuration -AgentAddress host IP addresses from DNS yes IP addresses of the agent hosts allowed in the firewall

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# minimal installation without SQL
.\Install-ObservabilityStack.ps1 -SqlServer '' -NonInteractive

# full all-in-one installation (prompts for passwords)
.\Install-ObservabilityStack.ps1 -SqlServer 'localhost,1433' -SqlLogin svc_obs_mssql_exporter `
    -WebconSqlReaderLogin svc_obs_grafana_reader -GrafanaListenAll -ConfigureWebcon

# no prompts (passwords from variables)
$exp = Read-Host 'Exporter password' -AsSecureString
$rdr = Read-Host 'Reader password' -AsSecureString
.\Install-ObservabilityStack.ps1 -SqlServer 'localhost,1433' -SqlLogin svc_obs_mssql_exporter -SqlPassword $exp `
    -WebconSqlReaderLogin svc_obs_grafana_reader -WebconSqlReaderPassword $rdr -NonInteractive

docs.title: Grafana in 10 minutes
docs.text: This chapter is for people who know WEBCON but have never used Grafana. After reading it, you will be able to open a dashboard, set the time range, filter the data, and go from a chart to the details of a single operation.

docs.title: Sign-in and navigation
docs.text:
1. Open Grafana – on the server http://localhost:3000, from another computer the address provided by your administrator (e.g. http://server:3000).
  2. Sign in with the account provided by your administrator (the Viewer role is enough for viewing).
  3. After signing in, you will see the Start screen (home dashboard, house icon): WEBCON status for the last 30 minutes in eight tiles, links to dashboards and documentation, and a list of active alerts. Clicking a tile opens “WEBCON – Performance”.

In the screenshot: Portal without traffic (gray / green tiles), Service alive = NO, and an active alert W4 No Service heartbeat – the WEBCON WorkFlow Service was running, but after the virtual machine was paused it stopped executing its work loop; fix: restart the WebCon WorkFlow Service service. 4. All dashboards: menu (☰, top left corner) → Dashboards. They are organized in folders:

Folder Dashboard Question it answers webcon WEBCON – Performance What is happening now, and where does the application lose time? webcon WEBCON – Operations What did the last week look like? Which actions and paths are the slowest, who has the most tasks, are external APIs working? webcon WEBCON – Availability and backlog Is the Portal responding, and is work piling up in the content database (timeouts, cyclical actions, emails)? sql SQL Server – WEBCON Is the database a bottleneck? host Windows – Host load Is the server short on CPU, memory, disk? dotnet ASP.NET Core technical details of the Portal (Grafana community dashboards)

Each dashboard has links to the others in the top right corner (the time range is carried over with the link) and a Documentation link to the description of its panels.

Start with WEBCON – Performance; a guide from symptom to cause: Scenarios.

docs.title: Time range (top right corner)
docs.text:
• Click the clock (e.g. Last 6 hours) and select a range or enter your own (now-2d → now, or specific dates).
  • Zooming in: select a part of a chart with the mouse (drag horizontally) – the whole dashboard switches to that range. To go back: the ⟵ button (Zoom out) or select the range again.
  • “Dashboard time range” tiles (e.g. Successful transitions, Service queue errors) count over the entire selected range – their value changes when you change the range.
  • The ⟳ arrow next to the clock refreshes the data; the drop-down list sets automatic refresh.

Time in Grafana is shown in your browser's time zone. Daily charts on the “WEBCON – Operations” dashboard count UTC days.

docs.title: Variables (filters at the top)
docs.text:
The drop-down lists below the title filter all panels at once, e.g.:

Dashboard Variable Meaning WEBCON – Performance / Operations Service Portal (web application), WebCon.WorkFlow (WEBCON WorkFlow Service), or both WEBCON – Performance Database (DB ID) WEBCON content database (installation with several content databases) Windows – Host load Host, Processes the server and the processes shown on the process charts SQL Server Databases databases on the per-database charts

docs.title: Panels
docs.text:
Type Appearance How to read it Tile (stat) large number, background color green = OK, yellow / orange = warning, red = problem. Color thresholds are described for each dashboard Line chart lines over time hover to see the values at a point; click a name in the legend to show only that series (Ctrl+click = add another one). Wider charts show mean / max / last values in the legend; narrow charts (three in a line) show only the series names – the values are in the tooltip Heatmap colored rectangles vertical axis = duration, color = how many operations took that long at a given moment; a bright cell high up = many slow operations Table rows and columns click a header to sort; blue (underlined) values are links – usually to traces Logs list of records click a record to expand its details (fields, trace_id)

Each panel has an ⓘ icon in its header (panel description – what it shows and how to read it) and a ⋮ menu: - View (v key) – panel in full screen, - Explore – opens the panel query in exploration mode (for advanced users), - Inspect → Data – panel data in a table, with the option to download a CSV.

“No data” in a panel usually means that the event has not occurred (e.g. Service queue errors appear only after the first error), not a failure.

docs.title: Three kinds of data
docs.text:
The stack collects three kinds of information about WEBCON – and lets you move between them:

Kind What it is WEBCON example Where Metrics numbers collected every minute: how many, how fast, how much 12 path transitions /min, Portal response time p95 0.8 s charts and tiles Traces the course of a single operation step by step, with durations form open: model 120 ms, rules 340 ms, REST data source 2.1 s, SQL 80 ms “Where the time goes” tables, trace view Logs messages written by WEBCON Error getting data for DataSource name: Exchange rates ID: 58 log panels

Details of the concepts: Concepts.

docs.title: Drilling down: from chart to root cause
docs.text:
This is the most important skill. A typical path:

red tile ─► chart (when?) ─► exemplar point or table (which operation?) ─► trace (which step?) ─► logs (what error?)

docs.title: 1. Exemplar – from a chart to a trace
docs.text: On duration charts (e.g. Portal response time, Path transition time) you can see small points (diamonds) – these are exemplars: sample individual requests from a given moment. Hover over a point high on the chart (a slow request) and click Query with Tempo / View trace – the trace of that request opens.

docs.title: 2. Table – from a ranking to traces
docs.text: In the “Where the time goes” tables (paths, rules, data sources, actions), click an identifier (e.g. a path ID) – a list of traces in which this operation occurred opens. Select a trace (e.g. the longest one).

docs.title: 3. Trace view
docs.text:
Portal: GET /api/nav/db/1/app/5/element/1234/form          2.8 s ████████████████████████████
  webcon.elements_management.element.model.load            2.5 s   ██████████████████████████
    webcon.rule.execute (rule.id = 18)                     0.3 s     ███
    webcon.data_source.data.load (data_source.id = 58)     2.1 s        █████████████████████
      HTTP GET api.nbp.pl                                  2.1 s        █████████████████████
    SELECT [WFElements]                                    0.05 s                           █
  • Each row is a span – one step of the operation; indentation = a step inside the parent step.
  • Bar length = duration. Look for the longest bar deepest in the tree – it is usually the cause (here: data source 58 calling an external API).
  • Click a span to see its attributes: webcon.rule.id, webcon.data_source.id, webcon.path.id, webcon.user.login, http.route, db.query.text (SQL query text), etc. The identifiers correspond to the IDs in WEBCON Designer Studio.
  • A red marker next to a span = error (e.g. HTTP 500 from an external API).

docs.title: 4. From a trace to logs and from logs to a trace
docs.text:
• In the trace view, the logs icon next to a span (Logs for this span) shows WEBCON logs with the same trace_id.
  • In a log panel, expand a record – the Open trace button next to the trace_id field opens the trace in which the log was written.

docs.title: Explore – your own questions (optional)
docs.text:
Menu → Explore is a free-form query mode. Useful even without knowing the query languages:

  • Tempo → Search: filter by service name (Portal), span name, duration (> 2s) – a list of traces.
  • Loki → Label browser / builder: select service_name = Portal, level error – a list of errors.
  • Sample TraceQL queries (Tempo):
{ name = "webcon.data_source.data.load" && span.webcon.data_source.id = 58 }      # calls of data source 58
{ name = "webcon.elements_management.path.transitions" && duration > 5s }          # path transitions longer than 5 s
{ span.webcon.user.login =~ ".*smith.*" && kind = server }                         # requests of a user

IDs in WEBCON are numbers – in TraceQL, use them without quotes.

docs.title: What Grafana does not do here
docs.text:
• Dashboards are read-only: changes to dashboards in the webcon, sql, host folders are lost when the stack is upgraded. For your own dashboard: Save as a new one.
  • Alerts do not send emails or messages – they are visible only in Grafana: Alerts.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Concept Meaning Example Metric a number measured over time, collected every minute number of path transitions, Portal response time Counter a metric that only increases (since the process start); charts show its increase webcon_elements_management_path_transitions_all_total … /s, … /min rate – how many events per second / minute, averaged over a window of several minutes 12 transitions /min Increase in the range how many events occurred in the entire selected time range (“dashboard time range” tiles) 3 Service queue errors in the last 6 h Histogram distribution of durations: how many operations took 0–100 ms, 100–250 ms, … – percentiles are calculated from it path transition time p50 (median) half of the operations were faster than this value – the “typical” time p50 = 0.3 s p95 95% of operations were faster, 5% slower – the time experienced by one user in twenty. The primary performance measure in these dashboards p95 = 2 s → 1 in 20 opens takes more than 2 s p99 the slowest 1% of operations – individual extreme cases Trace a record of the course of a single operation (a Portal request, a path transition, a Service task) with the duration of each step opening the form of instance 1234 Span one step in a trace: name, duration, attributes, status; spans are nested webcon.rule.execute (rule 18) in element.model.load Attribute additional information in a span webcon.path.id = 11, db.query.text = SELECT … Exemplar a point on a metric chart linked to a specific trace – a bridge from the chart to the details a diamond on the response time chart Spanmetrics metrics (count, duration) calculated automatically from spans – this is why there are charts for rules, actions, and form stages even though WEBCON does not send such metrics traces_spanmetrics_latency_bucket{span_name="webcon.action.execute"} TraceQL metrics statistics calculated directly from traces in Tempo (“Where the time goes” tables) – they work for a range of up to 7 days; count, total time, average and max are exact path ranking Log a message written by WEBCON (Serilog), with a level and often with a trace_id Error getting data for DataSource … Log level Information, Warning, Error, Fatal Service (job, service) telemetry source: Portal (web application under IIS) or WebCon.WorkFlow (WEBCON WorkFlow Service) SQL filter threshold SQL query spans shorter than the threshold (1 s by default) are dropped so as not to flood the storage – traces show only slow queries Retention how long data is kept: metrics 15 days, traces 8 days, logs 7 days (default)

docs.title: How WEBCON maps to telemetry
docs.text:
What you do / what happens in WEBCON Metric (chart) Span (trace) Attributes / identifiers a user opens a Portal page http_server_request_duration_seconds (HTTP request duration) server span with http.route http.route, http.response.status_code, webcon.user.login opening an instance form webcon_…_element_open_total webcon.elements_management.element.model.load webcon.process.id, webcon.step.id path transition (button on the form, Service) webcon_elements_management_path_transitions_* (count, successful, duration) webcon.elements_management.path.transitions webcon.path.id = path ID (WFP_ID) business rule / form rule – (spanmetrics) webcon.rule.execute webcon.rule.id (name empty in 2026.2.5) data source (SQL, REST, SOAP, …) – (spanmetrics) webcon.data_source.data.load + HTTP / SQL span underneath webcon.data_source.id, webcon.data_source.type.name action (REST, “Start workflow”, …) – (spanmetrics) webcon.action.execute webcon.action.id, webcon.action.name external API call (REST action / data source) http_client_request_duration_seconds HTTP client span server.address, error.type WEBCON SQL query (longer than the threshold) – SqlClient span, e.g. SELECT [WFElements] db.namespace, db.query.text Service work (queues, timers, Solr) webcon_service_queue_*, webcon_timers_*, webcon_solr_queue_* webcon.service.activity, webcon.service.heartbeat webcon.service.role.name error in WEBCON – span with error status (not always) Error log with trace_id

Important: data source and action spans do not have an error status, even when the call failed – the error is visible in the HTTP span underneath (error.type) and in the logs. This is why data source errors are shown from logs, and action errors from HTTP calls.

The identifiers (path.id, rule.id, data_source.id, action.id, process.id, step.id) are the same IDs that you see in WEBCON Designer Studio (e.g. in the object properties). The “WEBCON – Operations” dashboard retrieves path and process names from the content database.

docs.title: Where data delay comes from
docs.text:
• WEBCON sends metrics every 60 s, and charts average over several minutes – a change in load becomes visible after 2–5 minutes.
  • Traces and logs are available after a few seconds.
  • The Portal under IIS is shut down by IIS after a period of inactivity – it then sends no metrics (gaps in the charts are not a failure).

docs.title: Limitations worth knowing
docs.text:
• p95 is approximate – calculated from a histogram (duration buckets), so it can be up to the width of a bucket off (spanmetrics: 1, 2.5, 5, 15 s). For exact measurements – see average / min / max and individual traces. Tables based on traces (TraceQL metrics) show average and max instead of p95: Tempo's buckets are powers of 2 (… 4.3 s, 8.6 s), so p95 = 8.59 s could mean a slowest execution of 6.3 s.
  • Little traffic = unreliable percentiles. p95 of 10 operations is practically the slowest of them. Always look at the “Calls” column.
  • Nested spans are counted multiple times in the “Total time” tables – a rule executed during form loading increases the total time of both the rule and the loading.
  • Tables based on traces cover up to 7 days (Tempo query limit and trace retention); a longer range = an error or truncated results. Over long ranges they are calculated more slowly.

docs.title: “WEBCON – Performance” dashboard
docs.text:
Folder: webcon · Default range: last 6 h · Refresh: every 1 min

Purpose: current diagnostics – is WEBCON running fast, and if not, where is it losing time: Portal, form, rule, data source, action, SQL, or Service.

Filters: Service (Portal, WebCon.WorkFlow = Service), Database (DB ID) (content database). Links (top right corner): Windows – Host load, SQL Server, Traces (Explore), Documentation.

Annotations (toggles next to the filters) – vertical lines on all charts:

Toggle Color Meaning WEBCON process start (enabled by default) orange start of a Portal / Service process (restart, IIS pool recycling, start after inactivity). Response time spikes right after the line are a “cold start” – cache loading Cache marked for refresh purple WEBCON marked the configuration cache for refresh (e.g. application publishing in Designer Studio) – subsequent requests reload the configuration

Rows from general to detailed:

Row Question Status Is there a problem? (at a glance) Portal – user experience How fast does the Portal respond, and which pages are slow? Forms and path transitions How many transitions, how long do they take, which form stage is slow? Where the time goes Which specific path / rule / data source / action? SQL from the WEBCON perspective Which SQL queries are slow? WEBCON WorkFlow Service Is the Service keeping up with queues, timers, indexing? .NET runtime Are WEBCON processes short on CPU / memory / threads? Logs What errors and warnings does WEBCON write?

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
Tiles – the status at a glance. Start with the colors.

Tile What it shows Thresholds What to do when it is not green Portal requests /s how many HTTP requests the Portal handles (excluding health check) – (informational) a reference point: a slow Portal under heavy traffic ≠ a slow Portal without traffic Portal HTTP p95 95% of Portal requests are faster than this value 🟢 < 1 s · 🟡 1–3 s · 🔴 > 3 s Portal row → Routes by total time table 5xx errors % of responses with a server error (selected services) 🟢 < 1% · 🟡 1–5% · 🔴 > 5% HTTP errors by route, Logs row Path transitions /min all path transitions (Portal + Service), including failed ones – Successful transitions successful / all transitions in the range 🔴 < 95% · 🟡 95–99% · 🟢 ≥ 99% a failed transition = a validation, rule, or action error; Logs row, transition traces Path transition p95 95% of transitions are faster than this value 🟢 < 2 s · 🟡 2–5 s · 🔴 > 5 s Paths – longest transitions table Users (since start) unique Portal users since the last start of the Portal process – with nightly IIS application pool recycling = users of the current day; a Portal restart (recycling, WEBCON upgrade) resets the counter Service queue /min items taken from Service queues – Service queue errors queue items whose processing failed (range) 🟢 0 · 🔴 ≥ 1 WEBCON WorkFlow Service row, Logs (service WebCon.WorkFlow) Solr – backlog growth added to indexing minus processed (range) 🟢 ≤ 0 · 🟡 1–99 · 🔴 ≥ 100 > 0 = indexing is falling behind; Solr – indexing queues Service alive whether the Service sent a “heartbeat” in the last 5 min 🟢 YES · 🔴 NO the Service is stopped or hung – check the WebCon WorkFlow Service service Process starts how many times WEBCON processes started in the range 🟡 ≥ 1 restart = cache loss, slower first requests; unplanned restarts – logs, event log

docs.title: Portal – user experience
docs.text:
Panel What it shows How to read it Requests /s by route group Portal traffic in groups: home page / navigation, form, reports / dashboards, tasks, other API which part of the Portal is used most often; a spike in one group = e.g. a report opened en masse Portal response time (p50 / p95 / p99) typical (p50), slow (p95), and extreme (p99) response time p50 rises = everything is slow (server, SQL); only p95/p99 rise = selected pages are slow. Points = exemplars – click a point high on the chart to open the trace of a slow request Portal response time distribution heatmap: how many requests took how long at a given moment bright cells high up = many slow requests; a single “streak” at the top = a recurring slow operation HTTP errors by route number of 4xx and 5xx responses per route 5xx = WEBCON error; 401 after a session expires is normal; 404 = missing resource / wrong link Routes by total time (dashboard time range) table of routes: count, p95, total time (count × average time), % of 5xx errors total time shows what loads the Portal the most – a route called 10,000 times at 0.2 s weighs more than one called 10 times at 5 s. Clicking a route opens the ASP.NET Core Endpoint dashboard Active requests and connection queue requests being handled and connections waiting in the server queue a growing queue = the Portal is not keeping up (not enough threads / CPU) – see .NET runtime Portal and form opens home page and instance form opens /s Portal users unique users since the last start of the Portal process the counter drops to zero at a Portal restart; with nightly IIS application pool recycling the peak before the drop = users of that day

Routes (http.route) are Portal address templates with parameters in curly braces (e.g. {controller=Home}/{action=Index}/{id?}), not specific addresses – all form opens of different instances go to one route. The specific instance ID and user are in the request trace.

docs.title: Forms and path transitions
docs.text: Panel What it shows How to read it Path transitions all, successful, and failed transitions /min failed > 0 – check the logs and the traces of failed transitions Successful transitions by kind breakdown: new instance (element_new), save only (only_save), call source (Portal, Service, API) whether the load comes from creating new instances, saves, or transitions from the Service (e.g. timers, “Start workflow”) Path transition time (p50 / p95 / p99) transition time (WEBCON histogram) points = exemplars – the trace of a specific transition Path transition time distribution heatmap of transition times Transitions in progress, history, model cache transitions in progress at a given moment, history writes /s, instance models in cache a growing number of transitions in progress = transitions are blocking (e.g. SQL locks) Form handling stages – p95 p95 of successive stages: model retrieval / loading, rules and default values, JS model build, save, transition, actions, data sources which form stage is slow Form handling stages (dashboard time range) table of stages: count, p95, total time the stage with the largest total time is the best candidate for optimization. Nested stages are counted multiple times (a rule in model loading increases both)

docs.title: Where the time goes (paths, rules, data sources)
docs.text:
The most important row for application optimization. The tables are calculated from traces (TraceQL metrics) or spanmetrics, for the entire dashboard time range (up to 7 days). Columns: Calls, Total time and the duration – in tables calculated from traces Average (Total time / Calls) and Max, both exact; in spanmetrics tables p95 (approximate). Clicking an ID in a table calculated from traces opens the spans of this object in Explore: Show spans slower than average or Show all spans (the list is not sorted by duration – click the Duration column header).

Panel What it shows Identifier Drill-down WEBCON spans by total time all WEBCON operations (webcon.*) sorted by total time span name the overall picture – what WEBCON spends the most time on in total Portal MVC pipeline (filters) authorization and Portal request filters span name long on_authorization = permission / application checks Paths – longest transitions transitions by path ID webcon.path.id (path ID in Designer Studio) click the ID → spans of this path's transitions → trace → what takes time (actions, rules, SQL) Business rules rule executions by ID webcon.rule.id click the ID → spans; the rule name is not sent in WEBCON 2026.2.5 – find the ID in Designer Studio Data sources data loads from data sources by ID and type (SQL, REST, …) webcon.data_source.id, type a slow REST data source = a slow external API; a slow SQL data source = a query to optimize Actions action executions by ID and name webcon.action.id, name Form loading by process and step form open time per process and step webcon.process.id, webcon.step.id which form (step) opens slowly Form JS model build – steps stages of the server-side form model build step name details for advanced users Slowest requests (traces > 2 s) recent Portal / Service requests longer than 2 s: route, status, user login Trace ID click the Trace ID → the whole trace

How to read the rankings:

  • High average, low count – a rare but slow operation (e.g. a monthly report). Affects few users.
  • Medium average, huge count – “death by a thousand cuts”: the most total time, the biggest gain from optimization.
  • Max much higher than average – single slow executions (e.g. a lock, a slow external system at one moment), not a constantly slow object. Open the spans slower than average.
  • Total time = count × average time – the best column for setting priorities.
  • Tables calculated from traces show no p95: Tempo calculates percentiles from buckets that are powers of 2 (… 2.1 s, 4.3 s, 8.6 s), so p95 could be almost twice the real value (e.g. 8.59 s when the slowest execution took 6.3 s).

Example: the Data sources table shows data source ID 66 (REST type), average = 21 s, count 40. Clicking the ID → span → trace → under the webcon.data_source.data.load span there is an HTTP span to 10.255.255.1 lasting 21 s with the error status connection_error – the target server does not respond, and WEBCON waits until the connection timeout. Solution on the application side: a correct address / timeout in the data source configuration.

docs.title: SQL from the WEBCON perspective
docs.text:
SQL queries executed by WEBCON – from its point of view (how long it waited for the database).

Panel What it shows How to read it Slow SQL queries (above the Alloy filter threshold) recent SQL queries longer than the threshold (1 s by default): table, database, full query text click the Trace ID → in which WEBCON operation (form, report, data source) the query was run Slow queries by operation slow queries grouped by name, e.g. SELECT [WFElements] which table / operation is most often slow SQL Server – load queries (batch requests), transactions, compilations /s details: SQL Server SQL Server – waits (top 5 categories) what SQL Server waits for the longest SQL Server – locks and memory blocked sessions, longest lock wait, deadlocks, Page Life Expectancy locks during slow transitions = transitions are waiting for each other

Queries shorter than the threshold are not recorded – no slow queries in the table is good news, not an error.

docs.title: WEBCON WorkFlow Service
docs.text: Panel What it shows How to read it Service queues – dequeued items by role items processed by Service roles (e.g. SolrElementQueue, UserSynchronization) /s which role is working; unknown roles = “role ” Service queues – errors by role failed processing of queue items any value > 0 requires checking the Service logs Service work time by role – p95 how long a unit of work of a role takes rising time = the role is not keeping up Timers and cyclical actions timers and cyclical actions in progress, and executions /min a large number of executions = a looping timer or a bulk operation Solr – indexing queues added (solid line) vs processed (dashed) elements, attachments, activities /min solid line permanently above the dashed one = the backlog is growing Solr – durations (p95) Solr queries, indexing, text extraction from attachments slow extraction = large / unusual attachments Database cache – refreshes configuration cache refreshes a spike after application publishing is normal; frequent refreshes = response time spikes Database cache – duration (p95) cache refresh duration Heartbeat and health check Portal / Service heartbeat and health check duration; errors on the right axis heartbeat errors = a problem with the database or with Portal ↔ Service communication

docs.title: .NET runtime
docs.text:
The state of WEBCON processes (Portal, Service) from the .NET side. Useful when everything is slow at once.

Panel What it shows When to react WEBCON process CPU CPU usage in cores (1 = one full core) close to the number of server cores = not enough CPU Memory: working set and GC heap process memory and .NET object memory steady growth without drops = possible leak / growing cache GC pauses % of time the application was paused by garbage collection > 5% = memory pressure GC collections by generation garbage collection frequency frequent gen2 = many long-lived objects (cache, large models) Thread pool threads and work items waiting in the pool queue a growing queue with a constant thread count = thread pool starvation (everything slows down) Exceptions and lock contention .NET exceptions /s and lock contentions /s a spike in exceptions = check the logs

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
Panel What it shows How to read it Logs by level number of log records by service and level an error spike = an event to investigate Errors and warnings Warning / Error / Fatal records expand a record – fields exception_message, RequestPath, AuthenticatedUserLogin; the Open trace button next to trace_id

Searching the logs: panel menu ⋮ → Explore and add a filter, e.g. |= "DataSource" (contains text).

docs.title: “WEBCON – Operations” dashboard
docs.text:
Folder: webcon · Default time range: last 7 days · Refresh: every 5 min

Purpose: a weekly overview for the person who maintains applications – how heavily the server is loaded, how many people use Portal, which actions and paths are the slowest (with names from the database), who has the most tasks, and whether external systems (APIs called by data sources and actions) are working.

Unlike “Performance” (current, technical diagnostics), this dashboard answers questions from a weekly review or a meeting with the process owner.

Filters:

Variable Meaning Service Portal, WebCon.WorkFlow (Service) Exclude ports ports excluded from the external API panels (default 4317|4318|8983 – WEBCON's own telemetry and Solr) Exclude hosts excluded hosts (default localhost and the WEBCON host IP addresses set by the installer – Solr, Service modules) WEBCON hosts names of WEBCON servers – Portal → Service calls are not “external”

Panels based on the content database (path names, tasks) require the WEBCON SQL data source – without it they show an error or only IDs (installation, option c).

docs.title: Host
docs.text:
Panel What it shows Thresholds CPU – average / CPU – maximum average and highest 5-minute CPU utilization during the week 🟢 < 70 % · 🟡 70–90 % · 🔴 > 90 % Memory – maximum highest physical memory usage 🟢 < 70 % · 🟡 70–90 % · 🔴 > 90 % Fullest disk / Free space (min) usage of the fullest volume (now) 🟢 < 80 % · 🟡 80–90 % · 🔴 > 90 % Disk latency – max worst average I/O latency during the week 🟢 < 20 ms · 🟡 20–50 ms · 🔴 > 50 ms – the disk slows down SQL and WEBCON CPU and memory trend during the week peaks at fixed times = cyclical jobs, reports, backup

Maximum in red, average in green = short peaks; check when they occurred (chart) and compare with Top 10 actions – average time per day.

Host details: Windows – Host load.

docs.title: Portal – visits
docs.text: Panel What it shows Notes Home page opens – today Portal home page opens since midnight Sign-ins – today sign-ins since midnight sign-in ≠ visit: a user with a remembered session does not sign in again Users since Portal start unique users since the last start of the Portal process with nightly IIS application pool recycling = users of the current day; a Portal restart (recycling, WEBCON upgrade) resets the counter. Several Portal nodes: the largest node Opens and sign-ins per day bars per day (UTC days) usage trend – working days vs weekend, rollout of a new application

docs.title: Actions – top 10
docs.text:
Panel What it shows Actions – top 10 by average time 10 actions (ID and name from Designer Studio) with the highest average time: count, average, median, p95, min, max Top 10 actions – average time per day average time of these actions on consecutive days

How to read the table:

  • Min / max are exact (from traces), median and p95 are approximate (histogram) – they can fall outside the min–max range; this is not an error.
  • Average ≫ median = most executions are fast, but very long ones occur (e.g. an external API timeout).
  • Min ≈ max, high = the action is always slow – a candidate for optimization (e.g. the action's SQL query, the API call).
  • Click the action ID → traces of executions – the trace shows what the action did (HTTP, SQL, subworkflow start).

Daily chart: an increase in the average time of a single action starting on a specific day = a change in the application (publishing) or in the external system.

docs.title: Paths – top 10
docs.text:
Panel What it shows Paths – top 10 by average transition time 10 paths with the highest average transition time, with the path, step, workflow and process name (from the content database) Top 10 paths – average transition time per day trend on consecutive days (path ID – names in the table)

Transition time covers everything that happens after the path button is clicked: validation, rules, actions on the path and on entering the next step, saving to the database. You break down a slow path in the trace (click the ID) – usually a single action or a single query is to blame.

docs.title: Tasks – current status
docs.text:
Data straight from the content database – the current status, independent of the selected time range.

Panel What it shows Active tasks number of active tasks and overdue tasks Users with the most active tasks top 10 users: tasks, overdue, group (assigned to a group – the login is then the group login)

Use cases: bottlenecks in processes (one person with hundreds of tasks), substitutions, cleanup after an employee leaves.

docs.title: External APIs called by WEBCON
docs.text:
Outgoing HTTP calls from Portal and Service: REST / SOAP data sources and actions, authentication, licenses. Internal calls (Solr, Service modules, Portal → Service) are excluded by filters.

Panel What it shows How to read it Target servers – top 10 by call count server, number of calls, p95, % errors, from how many services which external system is called most often and how fast it responds Errors by server and type number of errors by type error types – see below Calls per hour by server (top 10) traffic over time Errors per hour by server and type errors over time since when the external system has been returning errors p95 response time by server (top 10) response time in hourly windows slowdown on the API provider's side Data sources by total time data sources (ID, type): count, average, max (exact, from traces), total time click the ID → spans slower than average or all spans → trace with the HTTP call and the target server Data sources with errors errors fetching data from a data source (from logs): data source ID and name, service, count a data source to fix in Designer Studio or an unavailable external system. Show logs button – the error message Actions with HTTP call errors actions in which an HTTP call returned an error WEBCON can complete an action “successfully” despite an HTTP error – this is where you see it. Approximate count. Show traces button

Error types (error.type):

Value Meaning Typical cause 400–499 the external system rejected the request wrong address / parameters (404), missing permissions (401, 403) – data source / action configuration 500–599 error on the external system's side API provider outage / overload connection_error the connection could not be established server down, firewall, wrong port; duration ~21 s = connection timeout (the server does not respond), short = connection refused name_resolution_error host name not found in DNS typo in the address, missing DNS record

Note: a data source that receives a 404 response does not always write an error to the log (WEBCON returns an empty result) – it will not appear in Data sources with errors, but the error is visible in the HTTP panels above.

Example: server httpbin.org:443 – 120 calls during the week, 40 % errors of type 500. Actions with HTTP call errors points to action ID 6. This is a test action calling an address that always returns 500 – in a real application: report it to the API owner or fix the address in the action.

docs.title: “SQL Server – WEBCON” dashboard
docs.text:
Folder: sql · Default time range: last 1 h · Refresh: every 30 s

Purpose: whether the database is the cause of slow WEBCON – load, what SQL Server is waiting for, locks, disk, memory, database size – plus a list of slow queries sent by WEBCON.

Filter: Databases (per-database charts). Requires SQL metrics (-SqlServer during installation).

The dashboard describes the entire SQL Server instance. If other systems also run on the instance, their load is visible here as well.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Tile What it shows Thresholds / when to react Batches /s Batch Requests/sec – general measure of load reference point Connections active connections to the selected databases sudden increase = connection leak or traffic spike Page life expectancy how many seconds a data page stays in memory 🔴 < 300 s · 🟠 300–1000 s · 🟢 > 1000 s; low = not enough memory, many reads from disk SQL Server memory memory used by SQL Server Blocked sessions requests currently waiting for a lock held by another session 🟢 0 · 🟠 ≥ 1 · 🔴 ≥ 5 Deadlocks (range) deadlocks in the time range each deadlock = one WEBCON transaction was rolled back (an error for the user)

docs.title: Load
docs.text: Panel How to read it Batches and compilations /s compilations > 10 % of batches = plans are not reused (ad hoc queries, e.g. from SQL rules without parameters) Transactions /s by database which database (content, configuration, attachments) is the most loaded Active requests running / runnable / suspended requests; many suspended = waiting for a resource (locks, disk)

docs.title: Waits – what SQL Server is waiting for
docs.text:
The best way to determine what is limiting the database:

Panel How to read it Wait time by category wait seconds per second (sum across all threads); the dominant category = the bottleneck Average time per wait long individual waits with few events = sporadic but severe problems CPU pressure (signal wait %) consistently > 20–25 % = not enough CPU for SQL Server Category Meaning What to check Locks waiting for locks held by other transactions Locks row, long path transitions / actions Data I/O, Log I/O, Other I/O waiting for the disk (data files / transaction log) Database I/O row, disk latency on the host CPU CPU shortage (waiting for a scheduler / worker thread) CPU pressure, heavy reports Parallelism parallel query execution (threads of one query waiting for each other) heavy reports / queries without indexes; MAXDOP and cost threshold for parallelism Memory waiting for a memory grant Memory row Latch, Buffer latch contention for internal structures / pages in memory often tempdb or “hot” tables (e.g. bulk inserts) Network / client the client (WEBCON) receives results slowly large query results, e.g. reports without paging OS calls, Other remaining waits usually background; relevant only when they dominate

docs.title: Locks
docs.text:
Panel How to read it Blocked sessions number of blocked requests and the longest current wait (right axis); sampled every 30 s – short blocking may not be visible Lock waits /s lock requests that had to wait / timed out Deadlocks /min deadlock details: Extended Events session system_health in SSMS

Locks in WEBCON usually result from long transactions: path transitions with a slow action (an API call within the transaction), bulk operations, heavy reports.

docs.title: Database I/O
docs.text: Panel How to read it Average I/O latency by database good values: data files < 20 ms, log < 5 ms I/O operations /s by database, I/O throughput by database which database puts the most load on the disk

docs.title: Memory
docs.text: Panel How to read it SQL Server memory committed consistently below target = SQL has headroom; committed = target and low PLE = not enough memory Page life expectancy sharp drops = the buffer pool is being flushed by large scans (e.g. a report without an index) Memory grants and buffer cache Memory Grants Pending > 0 = queries are waiting for memory; buffer cache hits should be close to 100 %

docs.title: Database size
docs.text: Panel How to read it Data size, Log size size of database files Log usage 🟠 > 70 % · 🔴 > 90 %; consistently high with the FULL recovery model = no transaction log backups Database growth growth rate – space planning, effect of archiving Log growths frequent autogrow slows down writes – larger growth increment / initial size

docs.title: Slow SQL queries (WEBCON traces)
docs.text:
A table of SQL queries longer than the threshold (1 s by default) sent by WEBCON: database, full query text, Trace ID. Click the Trace ID → you will see in which WEBCON operation (form opening, report, data source, action) the query was executed and who triggered it.

This combines the DBA and application developer views: the DBA sees the query, the application developer sees which form / data source generates it.

docs.title: “Windows – Host load” dashboard
docs.text:
Folder: host · Default time range: last 1 h · Refresh: every 30 s

Purpose: whether the server (WEBCON, IIS, SQL Server) is short of resources – CPU, memory, disk, network – and which process consumes them.

Filters: Host (server; in remote mode several hosts), Processes (processes on the charts in the Processes row: WEBCON, w3wp, sqlservr, stack components).

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Tile What it shows Thresholds CPU average utilization of all cores 🟢 < 70 % · 🟠 70–90 % · 🔴 > 90 % Memory used physical memory in use (excluding cache the system can reclaim) 🟢 < 80 % · 🟠 80–92 % · 🔴 > 92 % Commit committed memory (RAM + page file) relative to the limit 🔴 > 95 % = risk of running out of memory (OutOfMemory) Processor queue threads waiting for CPU consistently > 2 × number of cores = CPU shortage Lowest free space lowest free space % across volumes 🔴 < 10 % · 🟠 10–20 % · 🟢 > 20 % Uptime time since system start unexpectedly short = server restart

docs.title: CPU
docs.text: Panel How to read it CPU utilization by mode user = applications; privileged = kernel, drivers, antivirus; high interrupt / dpc = hardware drivers / network Utilization per core one core at 100 %, the rest idle = single-threaded operation Processor queue like the tile, over time Context switches /s sharp increase under steady load = too many threads / lock contention Processes and threads steady growth of threads = thread leak in some application

docs.title: Memory
docs.text:
Panel How to read it Physical memory available = free + cache (standby) that the system releases on demand Commit vs limit commit close to the limit = out of virtual memory – more RAM or a larger page file Paging from disk (hard faults) the best signal of a RAM shortage: sustained page reads from disk Page faults / s all page faults (most are “soft” and harmless) Kernel pools steady growth of the nonpaged pool = driver leak

SQL Server by default takes almost all free memory – a high Memory used value on a server with SQL is normal, as long as there are no hard faults and SQL is limited by max server memory.

docs.title: Disks
docs.text: Panel How to read it Disk usage % of time the volume was servicing requests; consistently ~100 % = disk saturated Read / write latency SSD: < 5 ms good, > 20 ms problem – critical for SQL Server Disk queue requests waiting for the disk IOPS, Throughput operations and bytes per second Free space free space % per volume

docs.title: Network
docs.text: Panel How to read it Network traffic bits / s received and sent; dashed line (right axis) = adapter bandwidth utilization % Errors and discarded packets should be 0 TCP established connections, resets, retransmissions (right axis, %) – > 1 % retransmissions = network problems

docs.title: Processes (WEBCON, IIS, SQL Server, stack)
docs.text: Panel How to read it CPU per process process share of total CPU (100 % = all cores) – which process loads the server Private memory (working set) steady growth without drops = memory leak I/O per process disk and network operations Handles, Threads steady growth = leak Process What it is w3wp IIS application pool (the process hosting Portal) WebCon.WorkFlow.Bootstrapper Portal (under IIS) and WEBCON WorkFlow Service WebCon.WorkFlow.Service, WebCon.WorkFlow.Module.ServiceModuleRunner WEBCON WorkFlow Service and its modules sqlservr SQL Server alloy, prometheus, loki, tempo, grafana observability stack – usually a few % CPU and 1–3 GB RAM in total

docs.title: IIS
docs.text:
Panel How to read it Requests /s requests to IIS sites (all applications, not only Portal) Current connections active connections to the site Rejected async I/O requests /s should be 0

IIS panels are empty on a server without IIS (e.g. a SQL host in remote mode).

docs.title: Alerts
docs.text: Grafana checks 30 rules every minute and marks a problem as an alert. Alerts are visible only in Grafana – they do not send emails or Teams messages (this can be added later).

docs.title: Where to see them
docs.text: Location What is there Menu → Alerting → Alert rules all rules in two folders: WEBCON – alerts and Observability stack – alerts; the state of each rule Menu → Alerting → Active notifications currently firing alerts Menu → Alerting → Silences silences (e.g. for the duration of planned maintenance)

docs.title: Rule states
docs.text:
State Meaning Normal condition not met – everything is fine Normal (NoData) no data – e.g. a machine without SQL Server; this is not a problem (the rules intentionally do not alert when there is no data) Pending condition met, but not for long enough yet (e.g. the rule requires 10 min) Firing (Alerting) firing alert Error the rule could not be evaluated – usually Prometheus or Loki is not running (DatasourceError); affects many rules at once

Click a rule to see its description, current value, state history, and the View panel link to the dashboard panel it refers to.

Severity (the severity label): critical – respond immediately; warning – check within the day.

docs.title: WEBCON rules
docs.text: ID Alert When Severity What to do W1 Slow path transitions (p95) transition p95 > 5 s for 10 min (min. 10 transitions) warning Scenario: slow transition W2 Slow Portal (p95) Portal p95 > 3 s for 10 min (min. 50 requests) warning Scenario: slow form W3 Portal 5xx errors > 5 % of responses with a server error (min. 10 errors) for 5 min critical Performance → HTTP errors by route, Logs W4 No Service heartbeat the Service was running within the last 24 h, but has shown no sign of life for 10 min critical the WebCon WorkFlow Service service – status, event log; scenario. Service in the Running state while the alert persists (e.g. after a virtual machine was paused) = the Service work loop has stalled – restart the service W5 Heartbeat / health check errors heartbeat or health check ended with an error warning Service and Portal logs; database connectivity W6 Service queue errors a Service queue item was not processed warning Performance → WEBCON WorkFlow Service, WebCon.WorkFlow logs W7 Growing Solr indexing backlog > 1000 backlog items within 30 min and growing warning Solr – indexing queues; the Solr service W8 Data source errors ≥ 5 data retrieval errors from a single data source in 15 min warning Operations → Data sources with errors; scenario W9 External API call errors ≥ 10 HTTP errors to a single server in 15 min (without the WEBCON host, Solr and OTLP) warning Operations → External APIs called by WEBCON W10 Spike in log errors ≥ 50 errors in a service's logs in 10 min warning Performance → Logs

docs.title: Availability and database backlog rules
docs.text:
Dashboard: WEBCON – Availability and backlog. Rules D1–D3 work when content database metrics are enabled (-WebconDbMetrics).

ID Alert When Severity What to do B1 Portal unavailable the Portal /health probe (or an additional address) without a 200 response / Healthy status for 3 min critical HTTP code panel: 0 = no connection (IIS, DNS, certificate), 5xx / Unhealthy = WEBCON (e.g. no access to the configuration database), 401 = see Troubleshooting B2 Certificate expiring soon the address certificate expires in less than 14 days warning renew the IIS binding certificate D1 Overdue timeouts overdue timeouts have not dropped to zero for 30 min warning the Service is not picking them up – check alert W4 and the scenario D2 Failed emails increasing in the last 30 min, new emails appeared with ≥ 3 failed attempts (emails that have exhausted their attempts stay in the queue, so the increase is what counts) warning SMTP configuration, Service logs D3 Cyclical actions with errors cyclical actions whose last execution ended with an error for 30 min warning Designer Studio (cyclical actions), Service logs

docs.title: SQL Server and host rules
docs.text: ID Alert When Severity What to do S1 SQL deadlocks a deadlock occurred (15 min) warning SQL Server → Locks S2 Long SQL blocking sessions blocked for 10 min warning as above; scenario S3 SQL memory pressure (Page Life Expectancy) Page Life Expectancy < 300 s for 30 min warning SQL Server → Memory H1 High host CPU utilization > 90 % for 15 min warning Host → Processes – which process H2 Low host free memory > 90 % for 15 min warning Host → Memory H3 / H4 Low disk space / Critically low disk space < 10 % (H3, warning) / < 5 % (H4, critical) warning / critical free up space; logs, backups, temporary files

docs.title: Observability stack rules
docs.text:
These concern the tool itself – whether data is being collected at all.

ID Alert When Severity What to do O1 Stack component not responding an obs-* service stopped responding critical Troubleshooting O2 Host stopped sending metrics host metrics were present within the last 24 h, but have been missing for 10 min critical Alloy / agent on the host; after a paused VM is resumed, the alert is expected and clears by itself O3 No telemetry from WEBCON WorkFlow Service the Service was sending data (last 24 h), but has sent nothing for 15 min critical Service stopped? configuration overwritten by a WEBCON upgrade? (the Portal is not checked – under IIS without traffic it stops sending, which is normal) O4 Tempo - query errors trace queries end with an error warning corrupted Tempo index O5 / O5b Tempo - spanmetrics near series limit / Tempo - spanmetrics dropping series O5: > 80 % of the max_active_series limit for 15 min; O5b: series dropped because the limit was exceeded O5 warning / O5b critical a very large number of paths / actions – report to the stack administrator O6 Alloy - telemetry dropped or not sent Alloy does not accept or write data for 5 min warning Alloy logs (event log), disk space O7 Low disk space for stack data < 15 % on the C:\Observability\data volume critical shorten the retention or free up space

docs.title: Silencing
docs.text:
For planned maintenance (WEBCON upgrade, server restart):

  1. Alerting → Silences → New silence.
  2. Duration (e.g. 2 h) and a matcher, e.g. severity = critical or alertname = W4 No Service heartbeat.
  3. Comment (reason) → Save silence.

docs.title: Changing thresholds
docs.text: The rules are in the repository (config-templates/grafana/provisioning/alerting/) and are read-only in Grafana. Changing a threshold = changing the file in the repository and reinstalling (Upgrade).

docs.title: Scenarios – from symptom to cause
docs.text:
Step-by-step recipes for typical reported issues. Each one starts with a symptom (“users say that…”) and ends at a specific object in WEBCON Designer Studio (form, path, business rule, data source, action) or at a server resource.

Navigation basics (time range, exemplars, trace view): Grafana in 10 minutes.

docs.title: 1. Form opens slowly
docs.text:
Symptom: “Opening a request takes several seconds”. Alert W2.

  1. WEBCON – Performance, with a time range covering the reported moment (e.g. Last 3 hours; zoom in on the chart by selecting an area).
  2. Status row: is Portal HTTP p95 yellow / red? If so, the problem affects many users. If it is green, the problem is isolated (one form / user).
  3. Portal – user experience → Portal response time (p50 / p95 / p99) row: is p50 rising (everything is slow → step 7) or only p95 / p99 (selected operations are slow → step 4)?
  4. Forms and path transitions → Form handling stages (dashboard time range) row: which stage has the highest p95 – business rules and default values (rules_and_defaults.apply), JS model build, data sources?
  5. Where the time goes → Form loading by process and step row: find the process and step with the highest average or total time (process / step ID = Designer Studio). Click the ID → spans → trace.
  6. In the trace, look for the longest bar deepest in the tree:
  7. webcon.data_source.data.load – data source (attribute webcon.data_source.id) → scenario 3 if there is a slow HTTP span underneath; slow SQL span → the data source query needs optimizing,
  8. webcon.rule.execute – business rule (webcon.rule.id) – e.g. a rule executed for every row of an item list,
  9. SQL span (SELECT [...]) – the db.query.text attribute shows the query.
  10. Everything is slow: .NET runtime (CPU, thread pools, GC), dashboards Windows – Host load and SQL Server (links in the top right corner – the time range is kept).

Example (illustrative): the form of the “Verification” step opens in 4 s. Trace: element.model.load 3.9 s → rules_and_defaults.apply 3.6 s → 12 × webcon.data_source.data.load (data_source.id = 58, type WebServiceREST) at 0.3 s each. The REST data source is called separately for each of the 12 fields. Solution: a single data source call with cache, or fields filled in by a single business rule.

docs.title: 2. Path transition takes a long time
docs.text:
Symptom: “After clicking »Approve« it spins for a long time”. Alert W1.

  1. WEBCON – Performance → Status: Path transition p95.
  2. Where the time goes → Paths – longest transitions: the path ID with the highest average or total time. The name of the path, step, and process is shown on the WEBCON – Operations → Paths – top 10 dashboard (from the database).
  3. Click the path ID → transition traces → select the longest one.
  4. In the trace: under webcon.elements_management.path.transitions there are actions (webcon.action.execute, attribute webcon.action.name), business rules, and saving (SQL). The longest item is the candidate:
  5. REST / SOAP action – time spent in the external system (HTTP span under the action),
  6. “Start workflow” action / subworkflows – transitions in subworkflows,
  7. SQL – locks (scenario 5) or a heavy query.
  8. Operations → Top 10 paths – average transition time per day: since when has it been slow? Compare with the application publication date.

Tip: an action that calls an external API during a transition extends the database transaction – other transitions wait for locks. Consider moving the call to an asynchronous action / the Service.

docs.title: 3. Data source or REST action returns errors
docs.text:
Symptom: “The choice list is empty”, “The action did not send data to system X”. Alerts W8, W9.

  1. WEBCON – Operations → External APIs called by WEBCON (time range: day / week).
  2. Target servers – top 10 by call count: which server has errors (error %) and how long it takes to respond (p95).
  3. Errors by server and type – the kind of error:
  4. 404 / 401 / 403 – configuration in WEBCON (address, authentication),
  5. 500–599 – a problem on the external system side,
  6. connection_error ~21 s – the server does not respond (firewall, wrong IP address),
  7. name_resolution_error – wrong host name.
  8. Data sources with errors: data source ID and name → Designer Studio. Show logs – the full error message.
  9. Actions with HTTP call errors: action ID and name. Show traces – the trace contains the HTTP span with the address and response code.
  10. Errors per hour by server and type: since when? A sudden start = a change on the external system side or an application publication.

Example (dev test data): data source 66 – average 21 s, connection_error to 10.255.255.1 (an address that does not respond). Every opening of a form with this data source waits 21 s. Action 6 (httpbin.org/status/500) – 100 % 500 errors; WEBCON completes the transition despite the error, so the user does not see it.

docs.title: 4. Service is not processing
docs.text:
Symptom: “Timers are not executing”, “Search does not find new documents”, “User synchronization does not work”. Alerts W4, W6, W7, O3.

  1. WEBCON – Performance → Status: Service alive (red = the Service is not sending a heartbeat), Service queue errors, Solr – backlog growth, Process starts.
  2. Service alive is red: the WebCon WorkFlow Service service (services.msc) – stopped? Event log → Application / System. After the Service starts, the tile changes color within 5 min.
  3. The service is running (Running), but the heartbeat does not come back: the Service work loop has stalled. Observed after a virtual machine was paused (clock jump in the System log, source Kernel-General, event 1): the Service still responded to /health, but stopped sending heartbeats and executing timers. Fix: restart the service.
  4. WEBCON WorkFlow Service row:
  5. Service queues – errors by role – which role (e.g. SolrElementQueue, UserSynchronization),
  6. Solr – indexing queues – the “added” line permanently above “processed” = the backlog is growing,
  7. Timers and cyclical actions – executions /min (a sharp increase = a looping timer),
  8. Heartbeat and health check – errors = a problem with the database or communication.
  9. Logs: variable Service = WebCon.WorkFlow, panel Errors and warnings – the error messages.

docs.title: 5. Database slows down
docs.text:
Symptom: everything is slow, especially saving and lists / reports. Alerts S1–S3.

  1. WEBCON – Performance → SQL from the WEBCON perspective: Slow SQL queries (above the Alloy filter threshold) – which WEBCON queries exceed the threshold (1 s by default). Click the Trace ID → in which WEBCON operation (form, report, data source).
  2. Dashboard SQL Server – WEBCON (link in the top right corner):
  3. Waits (what SQL Server is waiting for) → Wait time by category – the dominant category:
    • Locks → the Locks row; the cause is usually long path transitions (scenario 2) or bulk operations,
    • Data I/O / Log I/O → the Database I/O row and disk latency in the host dashboard,
    • CPU → CPU pressure (signal wait %), heavy reports / queries without indexes,
    • Memory → the Memory row, Page life expectancy.
  4. Batches and compilations /s: compilations > 10 % = queries without parameters (e.g. SQL business rules that build the query text).
  5. Pass the query from Slow SQL queries to the DBA together with the context (form / data source from the trace).

docs.title: 6. An alert fired – what now?
docs.text:
1. Alerting → Alert rules → click the firing rule: description, current value, View panel – the dashboard panel it refers to.
  2. Determine the scope: since when (rule state history), whether it affects a single service / host (alert labels).
  3. Go to the scenario for the rule – the “What to do” table in Alerts.
  4. Planned maintenance? Silence the alert (Silences) instead of ignoring it.
  5. Many rules in the Error state at once = a problem with the stack itself (Prometheus / Loki) – Troubleshooting.

docs.title: 7. Weekly review (no reported issue)
docs.text:
Once a week, 15 minutes, dashboard WEBCON – Operations (7 days by default):

  1. Host: CPU / memory / disk maximums – are we approaching the limits?
  2. Portal – visits: usage trend (working days, new applications).
  3. Actions – top 10, Paths – top 10: are there new items on the list? Is the average time of any object growing (daily chart)?
  4. Tasks – current status: users with a large number of tasks / overdue tasks.
  5. External APIs called by WEBCON: new errors, growing p95 of providers.
  6. Alerting → Alert rules: alerts from the week (state history) – are the thresholds reasonable?

docs.title: “WEBCON – Availability and backlog” dashboard
docs.text:
Folder webcon, dashboard WEBCON – Availability and backlog (the Portal available and Database backlog tiles on the Start screen). It answers two questions:

  1. Is the Portal responding? – an HTTP probe every 30 s.
  2. Is a backlog building up in the database that the Service is not picking up? – a read from the content database every 60 s.

WEBCON telemetry (the WEBCON – Performance dashboard) shows what the Portal and the Service execute. This dashboard shows what is waiting – e.g. overdue timeouts when the Service has stalled.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text:
Panel How to read it Status Available / Unavailable for each checked address (the Address variable at the top) Certificate – days to expiry red < 14 days (alert B2), orange < 30 days HTTP code 200 = OK; 0 = no response (DNS, connection, certificate); 302 = redirect (e.g. to sign-in); 401 = WEBCON does not respond anonymously; 5xx = application error Response time, HTTP request phases probe time and its components: resolve (DNS), connect, tls, processing (application time), transfer Availability over time availability interruptions on the timeline

What is checked:

  • WEBCON Portal – the main Portal address (given during installation or taken from an IIS binding with a host name), path /health; shown in the panels as that address. The Available result requires a 200 response and the Healthy status – in doing so, WEBCON checks, among other things, access to the configuration database. The probe runs on the Portal server: it connects locally (port from the Portal address), verifies the certificate for the host name from the Portal address, and sends the Host: localhost header, because WEBCON 2026.2 responds anonymously on /health only locally. The probe does not check the path through DNS, a load balancer or a firewall – use additional addresses for that.
  • Additional addresses (installer parameter -ProbeUrl) – e.g. the production Portal, a load balancer; a 2xx code is required.

docs.title: Database backlog
docs.text: Panel How to read it Overdue timeouts timeouts of instances past their due time that the Service has not picked up yet. Briefly > 0 – normal (the Service picks them up periodically); persists for 30 min – alert D1 Cyclical actions with errors active cyclical actions whose last execution ended with an error (alert D3) New failed emails (30 min) how many emails with at least 3 failed attempts appeared in the last 30 min – > 0 = a sending problem, e.g. SMTP (alert D2) Emails by attempt count the email queue by number of sending attempts. Emails that have exhausted their attempts (usually 5) stay in the queue – a large constant number at 5 attempts means old, permanently failed emails, not a current problem Queued emails all emails waiting to be sent or retried Queue tables row counts of WEBCON queue tables (name contains QUEUE; excluding additional ZWEBCON_* tables outside the WEBCON schema) – a rising trend without drops = the queue is not being processed

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
Panel How to read it Instances – daily change growth in the number of instances (WFElements rows) during the day – net, i.e. created minus deleted Instances – total number of instances in the content database Log tables the largest log tables (name contains LOGS, excluding the DicLogSources dictionary; the administrative logs AdminWFEventLogs and AdminServiceLogs are in the configuration database, which the stack does not monitor) – candidates for archiving or cleanup

Table row counts come from SQL Server metadata (without scanning the tables), so they may differ slightly from COUNT(*).

docs.title: When panels are empty
docs.text:
• Availability – the Portal was not detected in IIS (the site is stopped, or the stack runs on a separate machine without an agent on the WEBCON host), or the site bindings have no host name and the installer did not get the Portal address (-PortalUrl). Smoke test: section “WEBCON and host data (informational)”, row Availability probes.
  • Backlog / Database – database metrics are not enabled (-WebconDbMetrics $true) or the exporter login lacks permissions (sql\grant-webcon-db-metrics.sql). Smoke test: row WEBCON database metrics. Details: Requirements – database metrics.
